text:
olivia: quick update — ran the adaptive microbatch admission probe overnight against rdm1-prod (g4dn). curious about decode-rate bucket shapes and KV cache churn we saw.

samir: saw similar. p50 steady, p99 jumped ~18% for long prompts >1200 tokens after the kernel flip. suspect kernel selection fallback cost.

jia: timeline? did the kernel change coincide with admission tweak?

samir: yes — we enabled kernel_selector:v2 + admission smoothing (token-budget headroom 1.25) at 00:15. regression starts ~00:30.

miguel: attaching profiler snippets, rough: 
```
# hot spots (decode loop)
copy_kv_cache  45% CPU stalls
kernel_dispatch 28% increased latency
tensor_copy 12% frequent small memcpy
```

noah: copy_kv_cache spike is concerning — microbatching increases KV hits but also causes more small copies. could be memory bandwidth / kernel mismatch.

jia: what about decode-rate buckets? did many requests flip buckets mid-decode? that can trigger kernel re-switches.

samir: yes we saw ~7% of streams cross from medium->slow bucket during generation which forces kernel selection at runtime. that's ugly.

olivia: can we try a hysteresis on bucket transitions? i.e. require sustained decode-rate change for N tokens before switching kernel.

miguel: implemented a 3-token hysteresis in a local patch; initial replay shows p99 drops back ~10% on the long prompts. will run longer.

noah: also worth experimenting with admission smoothing: instead of hard token-budget 1.25, use soft cap with exponential decay to avoid burst admissions that thrash KV.
jia: agree. soft cap would throttle new requests more gracefully and reduce KV churn.

perf-bot: perf-alert: nightly-run-1918765400 flagged regression in rdm1-prod between 00:30-01:00, metric: decode_latency.p99 +17%. linked run: https://ci.redwood/1918765400

samir: re-run plan: (1) deploy kernel_selector:v2 + hysteresis 3 tokens, (2) switch admission to soft-cap with 0.8 decay factor, (3) enable detailed KV copy counters for 6h.
olivia: schedule the canary for 02:30 — prefer low-traffic window. samir can you own the rollout?
samir: yes. will coordinate.
miguel: added a tiny patch to avoid memcpy for zero-length KV moves — small win but microbatches add up.

noah: long-term: we should consider classifying workloads by steady-state decode-rate (avg over first 32 tokens) to pick kernels and admission budgets up-front instead of switching mid-decode. less switching = less jitter.
jia: let's add an experiment: pre-classify by first-16 token decode-rate and pin kernel, compare to hysteresis approach.
olivia: good. add to ticket INF-5234 and capture perf thresholds we want (target p99 <= baseline+5%).

samir: logging note: collect fields: initial_decode_rate, bucket_history, kv_copy_ops, kernel_chosen_per_step. that'll help diagnosis.
miguel: ok will add metrics and a small dashboard tile.

olivia: thanks all — tag me if the canary shows anything odd. :thumbsup:
